observations.finding: 23/50 pathways significant at q<0.05; top effects: HEme metabolism down (SMD -0.877, q=0.00093), pancreas beta cells down (SMD -0.867, q=0.00093), allograft rejection up (SMD +0.739, q=0.00093), IL6/JAK/STAT3 up (SMD +0.673, q=0.0011), TGF-beta down (SMD -0.686, q=0.0061).

2/13 genes significant at q<0.05: PBRM1 depleted (freq 0.254 vs 0.575, OR 0.252, 95% CI 0.108-0.586, q=0.0174) and ATM absent (0.0 vs 0.15, OR 0.042, q=0.0174). BAP1 enriched (0.175 vs 0.05, OR 4.02, q=0.257) and VHL depleted (0.476 vs 0.65, OR 0.49, q=0.275) are nonsignificant.

16/49 continuous features significant at q<0.05, with higher-in-set VHL (delta 0.629), SETD2 (0.620), PBRM1 (0.613), BAP1 (0.596), chr3p (0.508). Gain/loss: chr14q loss enriched (0.540 vs 0.20, OR 4.69, q=0.0106); chr6p loss enriched (0.175 vs 0.0, q=0.052); VHL/SETD2/chr3p loss depleted (q~0.059-0.062).

biological_support.statistical_interpretation: Coherent multi-modality signal: RNA shows strong, directionally consistent pathway shifts; WXS shows significant PBRM1 depletion and ATM absence; CNV shows strong 3p/VHL/SETD2/PBRM1/BAP1 and chr14q-loss differences. Effects are large and adjusted-significant in RNA, WXS, and CNV.
biological_support.medical_interpretation: C0001 exhibits a distinct molecular profile with chromatin-remodeling gene (PBRM1) depletion, ATM absence, and 3p/14q copy-number patterns, alongside immune/inflammatory pathway upregulation. This is consistent with a biologically coherent subtype but does not by itself establish clinical significance.
limitations: WXS tested only 13 genes; BAP1/VHL differences nonsignificant.
Pathway and CNV findings are relative to the rest set, not an external reference.

cross_modal_consistency.medical_interpretation: C0001 shows cross-modal membership compatibility, but the small silhouette magnitudes and significant wsi/cnv dispersion indicate the separation is modest and not strongly defined by any single modality.
limitations: Silhouette values are very small; resampling reused existing SNF affinities.
